To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the purified recombinant fusion protein of S‐antigen (S‐ag), which was expressed in Escherichia coli bacteria, is capable of inducing experimental autoimmune uveitis (EAU), the animal model for human autoimmune uveitis.
the recombinant human S‐antigen protein is uveitogenic, but the uveitis is milder than that caused by the native S‐antigen.
recombinant human S‐ag is uveitogenic when used to immunize Lewis rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a recombinant S antigen vaccine for treatment of autoimmune retinal vascelitis.
the development of recombinant fusion protein technology to produce large quantities of purified human S antigen for the study of its immunopathogenic role in autoimmune uveitis.
the development of a novel approach to study the molecular basis of the autoimmune disease EAU, which is a model for human autoimmune uveitis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
recombinant human S‐ag is a potent uveitogenic antigen in Lewis rats.
the recombinant human S‐ag fusion proteins were found to be uveitogenic.
the rGST‐Sag fusion protein is an excellent candidate to be used as an antigen for immunotherapy of uveitis in humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the recombinant fusion protein was as potent as the native S‐ag protein in inducing EAU.
the S‐ag is the most important retinal antigen for the induction of EAU, and the α‐Td is not uveitogenetic in Lewis rats.
the S‐antigen‐specific autoimmune T cell response in EAU is directed primarily against linear epitopes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
recombinant SAG is a good antigen to study the immunology of SAG‐induced autoimmune uveitis in animal models.
recombinant S antigen fusion proteins can be used for immunization to induce experimental autoimmune disease in animal models.
we were able to induce EAU in Lewis Rats with purified recombinent fusion proteins of GST-S-Ag and GST-Transducin.
